Upvoat-Only Spam, and Why Now is the Time to Actually Consider the Message

Sure sounds pretty naive though. To fight against negativity is to fight against human nature, and this problem will likely persist as long as new users keep coming to this site. And it's not necessarily straightforward deciding what constitutes as "negativity".

Ok, I understand where you're coming from with this, but hear me out.

If what is broadcast is "this is a place for only positive conversation," then psychologically only those that WANT this kind of interaction will tend to flock there.

Now, there will still be those who come who want to create a negative environment. And it's easy to think we'd need to bring this kind of interaction down. But I really urge you to consider, realistically, what would encourage someone looking to bring others down to stay around when (a) this isn't an environment which encourages that behavior, and (b) other mediums (like Reddit) exist that more easily allow this behavior.

We cannot eliminate this behavior with downvoats. Reddit has already proven that theory wrong. So perhaps ignoring it will work. I think it's more in the spirit of the site, and I really, truly believe negativity cannot exist if it isn't not accepted or acknowledged.

I'm still skeptical though. "Positive" is a highly subjective judgement, and varies across the subverses. Clashes between subverses ideologies on "positive engagement" are very hard to avoid, making it pretty darn difficult to instill a site-wide culture. You already see subreddit mods having differing opinions on content moderation and user engagement. And not all of them even align with the "official reddiquette", so what are the odds that promoting a "Voaters' etiquette" would be any more successful?
